source.title: Calgary Data Desk daily build
source.publisher: Calgary Data Desk (Hassan Ali), from City of Calgary, Calgary Police Service, Government of Alberta, Statistics Canada and CMHC data

city_actual.label: City's total, shared by actual growth
city_actual.about: All of Calgary adds up to the City's own population estimate and forecast for that month, but growth is not spread evenly: each community is its 2021 Census count times one factor, plus the growth the growth model measured there (homes built since 2021). The factor spreads only what homes do not explain (more people per home since 2021, people in seniors' homes, residences and shelters, the Census undercount) over every community's 2021 count. Fast-building areas get their real growth; built-out ones grow less.
city_actual.note: Each ward is its communities (the ward holding most of each community's area). Rates are per 1,000 residents a year, using residents in the middle of the period, counted the way chosen in Settings. Traffic incidents are placed by their exact location; crime is the Calgary Police Service figure for each ward.

city_pace.label: City's total, one rate for all
city_pace.about: All of Calgary adds up to the City's own population estimate and forecast for that month. Communities built since 2021 keep their growth model count; every other community is its 2021 Census count grown by one factor, the same for all, so each keeps its 2021 share. The factor also brings in people the Census count of private homes leaves out (seniors' homes, residences, shelters), so its growth since 2021 reads about 3 points higher than real growth.
city_pace.note: Each ward is its communities (the ward holding most of each community's area). Rates are per 1,000 residents a year, using residents in the middle of the period, counted the way chosen in Settings. Traffic incidents are placed by their exact location; crime is the Calgary Police Service figure for each ward.

model.label: Growth model
model.about: The 2021 Census for each community, grown with the homes on the City's current property assessment roll (homes lived in x 2021 people per home). Follows the homes actually built.
model.note: Each ward is its communities (the ward holding most of each community's area). Rates are per 1,000 residents a year, using residents in the middle of the period, counted the way chosen in Settings. Traffic incidents are placed by their exact location; crime is the Calgary Police Service figure for each ward.

census2021.label: 2021 Census, no growth
census2021.about: Each community's 2021 Census count (May 2021), unchanged. This is how the City's own 311 ward dashboard counts (it divides by 2021 Census households). Undercounts fast-growing communities.
census2021.note: Each ward is its communities (the ward holding most of each community's area). Rates are per 1,000 residents a year, using residents in the middle of the period, counted the way chosen in Settings. Traffic incidents are placed by their exact location; crime is the Calgary Police Service figure for each ward.

tax.bylaw: Bylaw 9M2026, the 2026 Property Tax Bylaw (passed March 31, 2026)

budget.note: Operating spending is net of recoveries; capital is the capital budget for the year. "Approved" years are the budget Council approved (updated each November); "Actual" years are what was spent. The City publishes its budget by department and service, not by ward or community.
